items.note: Thirty participants generated design concepts with GPT-4 agents (IntelliStorm, EvoluTRIZ) or with human partners under brainstorming and TRIZ across two phases a month apart; fluency, elaboration, and originality were scored (originality favored human-human) plus electrodermal activity. Below 50 participants; assignment and order not stated.

Sixteen groups of five brainstormed with DALL-E or Miro, online or offline, in a 2x2 design; two raters scored fluency, elaboration, flexibility, and originality, and online DALL-E sessions produced more elaborated ideas. N of 80 is derived from 16 groups of five; the unit of assignment is the group and the method is not stated.

Two preregistered studies on advertising slogans: Study 1 compares ChatGPT-4 slogans with human slogans (higher quality, lower diversity), and Study 2 gives people GenAI assistance and finds higher slogan quality for less creative individuals but not for egocentric creators. Abstract taken from the PsyArXiv version (doi 10.31234/osf.io/uz2cm, 'Chat-GPT4 can Enhance Marketing Creativity'); SSRN record had no abstract; N not stated.

Framed field experiment in which innovation teams used a custom GenAI ideation tool or worked as a control group; AI teams produced higher-quality ideas faster with greater idea diversity. arXiv abstract gives no N or assignment; search notes report 70 students in 24 three-person teams, randomized per the Mendeley dataset page (unverified).

Scenario-based between-subjects experiment with 226 designers and design students varying the degree of creative control in designer-AI co-creation, with design creativity as the outcome via ownership and cognitive load mediators. It is unclear whether creativity is rated on a produced design or self-reported in a vignette; the next stage should check.

Ten in-person workshops (54 participants) evaluated co-designed AI interventions for team brainstorming in AI impact assessment; AI improved rated impact-assessment quality for a chatbot-companion use case but not for a kidney-allocation application. Comparison condition and assignment not described; same work as arXiv 2604.27997 (FAccT 2026).

Per search notes, compares GAI-assisted with traditional teaching during logo concept ideation for novice and skilled design students, with GAI raising quantity, novelty, and diversity of concepts but not design quality. Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Springer page, web search tried); N and assignment unknown; possibly intact classes.

Per a search snippet, Experiment 1 (170 students) varied whether students thought independently before or after collaborating with AI on a creative problem, and deeper integration of human ideas with AI output raised creativity. Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, ScienceDirect 403, web search); N of 170 is from the snippet and unverified; compares AI-use configurations.

Per search notes, a two-month course study in which engineering students used AIGC tools (n=54) or traditional methods (n=59) for creative problem solving, with pre and post Creative Engineering Design Assessment scores (fluency, flexibility, originality, usefulness). Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar elided, Crossref, Springer blocked, web search); groups may be intact; whether the post-test was done without AI is unknown (possible after_ai).

Mixed-methods classroom study in a college creativity course scoring AUT fluency, flexibility, elaboration, and originality to assess ChatGPT-3's effect on divergent thinking. Abstract states no comparison structure or N; search notes suggest students did the AUT first without technology and later with ChatGPT (likely a fixed-order within-person design, not randomized).
